text:
Jordan (Support): FYI we have a customer on eu-west-1 reporting a burst of 504/5xx errors starting ~12:34 UTC. They say ~30% of requests to /v1/generate returned 504 or timed out. Happening across multiple API keys.

Jordan (Support): Customer logs show retry loops, high latency, and high token counts per request. They attached a curl repro hitting our hosted endpoint: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-xl","input":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":2000}'
```

Alice K: Looking at infra metrics — request_queue_depth spiked to ~4800 at 12:34, our per-node queue limit is 5000 and we hit it in several zones; continuous-batcher latency distribution shows a huge tail (p99 > 6s). When queue depth hits limit we short-circuit with 502/504 to avoid OOM.

Alice K: Also seeing batching_window_ms increased to 200 in a recent runtime flag flip (we roll this per-release). That increased latency per batch and created backlog under bursty traffic.

Ben S: Confirmed from logs: many requests stuck waiting on batcher.acquire() and we see backlogMetrics { waiting: true, queue_len: 1200, worker_idle: 0 } across pods. Kubernetes events show kube-scheduler churn but not enough pod autoscale during the spike.

Carmen R: Customer reports traffic pattern: many parallel long-generation calls (2k tokens) coming from a single service. They hit us with concurrency ~150 req/s for a minute.

Darryl (oncall): Mitigation plan: 1) Reduce batching window back to 40ms globally for hosted cluster; 2) Increase REQUEST_QUEUE_MAX from 5000 -> 8000 as temporary relief; 3) Scale batcher pool by +3 replicas in eu-west-1. I'll do 1 & 3 now, then 2 if needed.

Ben S: Commands I recommend: 
```
# scale batcher deployment
kubectl -n redwood-prod scale deployment/batcher --replicas=6 --context=eu-west-1

# verify queue metrics
curl -s http://prometheus.redwood.svc:9090/api/v1/query?query=request_queue_depth | jq .
```

deploy-bot: deploy started by Darryl (oncall) for config/runtime/batching_window -> 40ms (canary on 10% lanes). :rocket:

ops-bot: alert: request_queue_depth eu-west-1 > 4000 (firing)

Alice K: Note: the root cause is the interaction of larger batching window + bursty long-token requests. Batching helps amortize compute for short requests, but with long sequences it increases per-request time and the queue backs up. Also we hit our queue depth safety cutoff which converts waiting requests into immediate 5xx to protect memory.

Jordan (Support): Customer wants ETA and workaround. Suggested they: 1) limit client concurrency to 10; 2) reduce max_tokens when possible; 3) implement client-side exponential backoff. They've already applied a throttling workaround on their side.

Darryl (oncall): Canary config change completed, telemetry shows p99 batcher latency dropped from ~6.3s -> ~1.1s on canary lanes. Rolling to 100% now. Scaling finished.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: runtime/batching_window=40ms rolled to 100% (revision r2026-03-15-09).

ops-bot: alert resolved: request_queue_depth eu-west-1 back to normal (median ~120). :white_check_mark:

Ben S: Follow-ups: (A) Add a sliding-scale batching window that shrinks automatically when per-request token length > 512 or when queue depth > 1000. (B) Add a queue-depth-based adaptive rejection policy with informative 429/Retry-After instead of opaque 502/504. (C) Add a dashboard for per-customer concurrency hotspots and token-length distributions.

Alice K: I'll file a runtime ticket for the adaptive batching behavior and add a unit test that simulates bursty long-token traffic. Also will add an alert-runbook mapping queue_depth -> mitigations (scale, shrink window, rate-limit).

Jordan (Support): Customer updated: errors subsided after we asked them to throttle; we'll follow up with postmortem and recommended client limits.

Carmen R: Repro steps for engineering: run locust with 150 rps, payloads ~1.5k tokens, concurrency 150, duration 2m. You should see queue growth and then 5xx when depth limit hit. I put the test spec in /docs/playbooks/batcher-load-test.md.

Darryl (oncall): Post-incident tasks: 1) Alice - runtime ticket for adaptive batching (P0) 2) Ben - implement graceful 429 with Retry-After (P1) 3) Jordan/Carmen - customer follow-up + recommended SDK backoff (P2). I'll owner the retro.

Jordan (Support): Thanks all. Flagging this for a postmortem in #postmortems after retro. :eyes:

-- end of thread --
